elements.scope_reason: This red box is a management box ('Give emergency contraception if ...'), not a 'give urgent attention' triage box, so the house standard's red-box-to-priority pattern does not apply directly. But the trigger is a criterion the language can express: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unprotected sexual intercourse" "finding")) with (< (onset ...) (time_ago 5 days)). 'Does not want pregnancy' has no SNOMED finding (searched 'does not want pregnancy', 'pregnancy not wanted': none), though 'Unwanted pregnancy' (finding) exists as a loose proxy. A check task 'Check pregnancy test' anchored on that trigger would be within the briefing's check_for pattern.
parts_missing: unprotected sex within the past 5 days (expressible: 'Unprotected sexual intercourse' finding + onset within 5 days)
does not want pregnancy (no exact concept; 'Unwanted pregnancy' finding is the nearest)
elements.problem: Nothing in the file refers to emergency contraception, unprotected sex or a pregnancy test; the page's only red box is entirely unencoded.

elements.scope_reason: Two parts. (a) 'Check pregnancy test' is a check step the page tells the health worker to perform, conditional on the box-header trigger; SNOMED has 'Urine pregnancy test' (procedure) and 'Pregnancy test negative'/'Pregnancy test positive' (findings), so a check task is expressible. (b) 'if negative, insert Copper IUD as soon as possible or give single dose levonorgestrel 1.5mg orally' is a management step (no manage tasks by design).
parts_missing: (a) check pregnancy test when unprotected sex in past 5 days (check task; not encoded)
elements.problem: Part (a) is not encoded. Part (b) is out of scope (management_step).

elements.scope_reason: management_step: the criteria (weight > 80 kg; BMI >= 30; on efavirenz, rifampicin, phenytoin or carbamazepine) only select a dose/method of emergency contraception. With no manage tasks there is nothing to consume them, and a check_for with no consumer fails test constraint 2. Also BMI is not_representable (no unit) and the grammar has no medication atom, so 'on efavirenz' would need a finding/situation concept (only substance/product concepts were found).
management_step: on ketoconazole/fluconazole -> counsel about nausea/vomiting and offer Copper IUD instead. Drug-interaction advice selecting a method; no diagnostic or triage conclusion.
management_step: vomiting < 2 hours after levonorgestrel -> repeat dose. A dosing instruction.
management_step: offer long-term contraceptive at the same visit; follow-up pregnancy test in 2 weeks if injectable/implant given. Both are management/follow-up instructions.

cross_reference_only: 'Check for symptoms of STIs: vaginal discharge, ulcers, lower abdominal pain. If present -> 62.' The diagnostic logic for those symptoms is on page 62; this page draws no conclusion of its own. A check_for of these on this page would have no consuming rule in this file.

cross_reference_only: a list of conditions (cancer, blood clots, hypertension, stroke, IHD, diabetes, liver disease, migraines, unexplained vaginal bleeding) that send the reader to the method-suitability table on page 172. No diagnosis or priority on this page.

cross_reference_only: ask about menopausal symptoms if > 40 (yearly); 'if menopausal -> 187'. The menopause diagnosis is made on page 187; SNOMED 'Menopausal symptom' (finding) exists if a builder wanted a check task, but nothing on this page would consume it.

not_representable (BMI has no unit in the language, so 'BMI >= 25' cannot be a measurement comparison) and cross_reference_only (-> 156).

Three parts. (1) 'Check BP: if >= 140/90 -> 148' is cross_reference_only (hypertension is diagnosed on 148). (2) 'known hypertension or BP >= 140/90 -> avoid/change from combined oral contraceptive' and (3) 'BP >= 160/100 -> also avoid/change from injectable' are contraceptive-method management decisions. The thresholds themselves are fully representable (BP is a routine vital in mmHg; 'known hypertension' = active_condition), so a strict reader could expect them encoded; the conclusion, however, is a management step the house standard leaves out, and there is no diagnosis to attach them to.
parts_missing: (2) known hypertension or BP >= 140/90 while on combined oral contraceptive
elements.problem: Not encoded; defensible as management_step, but the thresholds are expressible and a builder could reasonably have recorded them. Low consequence.

elements.scope_reason: cross_reference_only: check for lumps in breasts (-> 55) and axillae (-> 42). The diagnostic logic is on those pages; a check_for here would have no consumer in this file.

'If pregnancy suspected (nausea/breast tenderness/missed period when using combined oral contraceptive), check for pregnancy' is a 'suspect X' with explicit discriminating findings: a check task plus a possible diagnosis of Pregnancy is exactly the house pattern. 'Before starting contraception ... check for pregnancy' is a second trigger for the same check.
parts_missing: 'Before starting contraception' -> check for pregnancy: not encoded. Both the task and the rule are gated on (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")), so a patient who is not yet on contraception never triggers the pregnancy check.
elements.problem: The 'pregnancy suspected on COC' half is encoded correctly: all five concepts exist exactly (Uses combined oral contraception 268458002, Nausea 422587007, Tenderness of breast 55222007, Missed period 36521000, Pregnancy 77386006); the or-of-three symptoms and the 'possible' level match the page's 'if pregnancy suspected'. Minor reading choice: the page's 'when using combined oral contraceptive' most naturally qualifies 'missed period' (amenorrhoea on injectables is expected) but could be read as qualifying all three; the rule gates all three on COC, which is the narrower reading and will not fire for nausea/breast tenderness in a patient on another method. The 'before starting contraception' branch has no SNOMED hook here either (no 'starting contraception' concept found), but it is a page trigger the rule lost.
evidence: Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive :: (task "Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive" adult (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")) (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Nausea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenderness of breast" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Missed period" "finding"))))

Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive :: (system_diagnosis_rule "Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive" (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Pregnancy" "finding") possible) adult (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Nausea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenderness of breast" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Missed period" "finding")))))

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive / Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive
rule_level_problems.problem: The page's pregnancy check has two triggers: 'before starting contraception' and 'if pregnancy suspected on COC'. Both the task and the rule are anchored only on 'Uses combined oral contraception', so the first trigger is lost and a new patient (the one most in need of a pregnancy check before a method is started) never reaches the check.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive
rule_level_problems.problem: The task's only trigger is (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")), which nothing in this file records and which is not a common symptom, warning sign or routine vital. Unless intake or another page records that finding, the task and therefore the rule will never fire (Will's briefing, 'Anchoring due_to so rules actually fire').

The page's only red box (emergency contraception) has no rule at all. It is a management box rather than a 'give urgent attention' box, so no priority evaluation is owed, but its trigger ('unprotected sex in past 5 days') and its first step ('check pregnancy test') are expressible as a check task with 'Unprotected sexual intercourse' + onset within 5 days, and the house standard expects every red box to be represented as check tasks where the language allows.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive
rule_level_problems.problem: The COC gate is applied to all three symptoms. On the page, 'when using combined oral contraceptive' reads most naturally as qualifying 'missed period' only; nausea or breast tenderness in a patient on an injectable or implant would also be 'pregnancy suspected' but will not trigger the rule. Narrower than the page, not wrong.

summary: The one in-scope diagnostic element (suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraception) is encoded with exact, verified SNOMED concepts and the right or-logic and possible level, but it loses the page's other trigger, 'before starting contraception', and its only anchor ('Uses combined oral contraception') is a finding nothing in the file records, so the task may never fire. The emergency-contraception red box is entirely unencoded; most of it is management by design, but its trigger and the 'check pregnancy test' step are expressible as a check task. The BP thresholds for avoiding COC/injectable are expressible but lead only to management decisions, so their omission is defensible.
